PROCEDURE PERFORMED:
Ion robotic bronchoscopy
INDICATIONS:
1.9 cm right upper lobe apical indeterminate lung mass; underlying rheumatoid arthritis. Tissue diagnosis requested.
MEDICATIONS:
General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway
IMAGING / CONFIRMATION:
DT; radial EBUS
TECHNICAL DIFFICULTY:
No
LIMITATIONS:
None
TOLERANCE:
Good after intervention
FINDINGS:
After informed consent and time-out, a therapeutic bronchoscope was introduced under general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway. Airway inspection to the
first subsegmental level showed no obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic platform was docked and a deliberate workflow with fluoroscopy, radial
EBUS, and cone-beam confirmation was performed. The target was a 1.9 cm lesion in the right upper lobe apical. Imaging confirmation used DT. Initial
fluoroscopy suggested near-target positioning. Radial probe EBUS demonstrated subtle concentric signal after catheter adjustment. A cone-beam or
tomographic spin was then obtained to assess tool-to-lesion relationship, after which the catheter was adjusted as needed and repeat fluoroscopy was
performed. Once tool-in-lesion or satisfactory tool-to-lesion relationship was confirmed, lesion sampling proceeded. Samples obtained included TBNA x5;
forceps biopsies x7; brushings x2; BAL x1; cryobiopsies x3. Technical difficulty: No. Limitation(s): None. Associated linear EBUS staging was then performed.
Surveyed stations included 11L (5.8 mm), 4L (6.4 mm), 7 (10.1 mm), 4R (7.2 mm). Sampled stations: 11L x4 (malignant cells on ROSE); 4L x3 (negative on
ROSE); 7 x4 (negative on ROSE). At the end of the case, the airway was reinspected, blood/secretions were suctioned, and there was no active bleeding.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS:
<5 mL
COMPLICATIONS:
Brief bronchospasm treated with bronchodilator and deepening of anesthesia
IMPRESSION:
Successful ion robotic bronchoscopy targeting of the right upper lobe apical lesion. Associated EBUS staging was
performed. Minor immediate complication: brief bronchospasm treated with bronchodilator and deepening of
anesthesia.
RECOMMENDATIONS:
Recover in PACU; post-procedure chest radiograph per protocol; await final pathology; integrate EBUS staging into
treatment planning
CPT / ICD:
Synthetic only / synthetic only
Ion robotic bronchoscopy report

PATIENT: SYNTHETIC PATIENT 19  MRN 9923000019  DOB 08/02/1978
PROCEDURE: Ion robotic bronchoscopy
INDICATION: 3.0 cm left lower lobe posterior basal PET-avid lesion; prior treated lung cancer. Tissue diagnosis requested.
ANESTHESIA: General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway
After informed consent and time-out, a therapeutic bronchoscope was introduced under general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway. Airway
inspection to the first subsegmental level showed no obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic platform was docked and a deliberate workflow
with fluoroscopy, radial EBUS, and cone-beam confirmation was performed. The target was a 3.0 cm lesion in the left lower lobe posterior basal. Imaging
confirmation used DT. Initial fluoroscopy suggested near-target positioning. Radial probe EBUS demonstrated blunted eccentric radial signal. A
cone-beam or tomographic spin was then obtained to assess tool-to-lesion relationship, after which the catheter was adjusted as needed and repeat
fluoroscopy was performed. Once tool-in-lesion or satisfactory tool-to-lesion relationship was confirmed, lesion sampling proceeded. Samples obtained
included TBNA x5; forceps biopsies x10; brushings x2; BAL x1; cryobiopsies x3. Technical difficulty: No. Limitation(s): None. Associated linear EBUS
staging was then performed. Surveyed stations included 7 (10.1 mm), 4R (7.2 mm), 11R (8.9 mm), 10R (7.4 mm). Sampled stations: 7 x4 (malignant
cells on ROSE); 4R x3 (negative on ROSE); 11R x4 (negative on ROSE). At the end of the case, the airway was reinspected, blood/secretions were
suctioned, and there was no active bleeding.
EBL: <5 mL
COMPLICATIONS: Post-biopsy airway oozing, controlled with dilute epinephrine saline
IMPRESSION: Successful ion robotic bronchoscopy targeting of the left lower lobe posterior basal lesion. Associated EBUS staging was performed. Minor
immediate complication: post-biopsy airway oozing, controlled with dilute epinephrine saline.
PLAN: Recover in PACU; post-procedure chest radiograph per protocol; await final pathology; integrate EBUS staging into treatment planning

text:
Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy with peripheral lesion biopsy and linear EBUS-TBNA. The indication was indeterminate pulmonary nodule with elevated clinical probability of malignancy. Preprocedure CT demonstrated a 28-mm ground-glass LUL target associated with a subtle bronchus sign and located about 18 mm from the pleural surface.

After informed consent and a procedural time-out, the patient was placed under general anesthesia with a cuffed endotracheal tube. The tracheobronchial tree was inspected to the first subsegmental level. No endobronchial mass was identified. Ventilation was adjusted to limit atelectasis during navigation, with recruitment performed before advanced imaging. Using shape-sensing navigation, the catheter was advanced through LB1+2 apicoposterior to within approximately 2 mm of the planned lesion center. Fixed cone-beam CT (CBCT) was obtained before biopsy. The initial spin showed CT-to-body divergence of approximately 5 mm. The target was updated, the catheter was adjusted, and a repeat limited spin confirmed the biopsy tool coursing through the lesion. Radial EBUS was not used for this target. Tissue acquisition included 7 passes of transbronchial needle aspiration with a 21-gauge flexible needle, 2 1.1-mm transbronchial cryobiopsies, and bronchoalveolar lavage from the target segment (40 mL instilled, 16 mL returned). ROSE showed lesional cells suspicious for malignancy.

After peripheral sampling, linear EBUS was performed. Stations 11R, 4R, 7, 4L, 11L were identified and sampled with multiple needle passes where anatomically accessible. Nodal staging was completed in a systematic N3-to-N1 sequence relative to the target side.

Hemostasis was excellent. The patient tolerated the procedure without immediate complication.

Impression: Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 28-mm ground-glass LUL lesion with tissue acquisition. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated CBCT, with tool-in-lesion confirmation documented. Systematic EBUS-TBNA staging was performed (11R, 4R, 7, 4L, 11L). No immediate complication.

PROCEDURES PERFORMED: Shape-sensing robotic bronchoscopy (Ion) with transbronchial biopsy and linear EBUS-TBNA.
INDICATION: peripheral pulmonary opacity requiring tissue diagnosis before definitive therapy.
TARGET: Preprocedure CT demonstrated a 33-mm ground-glass RML target associated with a positive bronchus sign and located about 18 mm from the pleural surface.

DETAILS: After informed consent and a procedural time-out, the patient was placed under general anesthesia via an 8.5-mm ETT. The tracheobronchial tree was inspected to the first subsegmental level. No endobronchial mass was identified. PEEP and tidal volume were optimized for peripheral navigation, and a breath hold was coordinated for 3D imaging. Navigation proceeded to the peripheral RB4 lateral airway. The catheter was locked after the system indicated proximity to the target. Intraprocedural CBCT was used for localization. Multiplanar reconstructions demonstrated the catheter adjacent to the target; after a 6 mm correction, needle position was confirmed within the lesion. Radial EBUS demonstrated an eccentric lesion pattern; the catheter was repositioned toward the maximal ultrasound signal before sampling. Tissue acquisition included 5 passes of transbronchial needle aspiration with a 21-gauge flexible needle, 2 1.1-mm transbronchial cryobiopsies, and bronchoalveolar lavage from the target segment (40 mL instilled, 20 mL returned). ROSE showed atypical epithelial cells; additional material was obtained for cell block and molecular testing.

STAGING: After peripheral sampling, linear EBUS was performed. Stations 11L, 7, 4R, 11R were identified and sampled with multiple needle passes where anatomically accessible. Nodal staging was completed in a systematic N3-to-N1 sequence relative to the target side.

COMPLICATIONS: No immediate procedural complication occurred. The patient was extubated in the procedure area and transferred to recovery in stable condition.

FINAL IMPRESSION: Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 33-mm ground-glass RML lesion with tissue acquisition. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated CBCT, with tool-in-lesion confirmation documented. Systematic EBUS-TBNA staging was performed (11L, 7, 4R, 11R). No immediate complication.

# SYNTHETIC BRONCHOSCOPY REPORT 46 — NG-SYN-046

**Synthetic patient:** 51-year-old man  
**Indication:** Evaluation of a 8-mm spiculated solid pulmonary lesion in the RUL posterior segment (RB2); bronchus sign present; lesion was moderately FDG-avid.  
**Preprocedure diagnosis:** Peripheral pulmonary lesion requiring tissue diagnosis.  
**Postprocedure diagnosis:** 8-mm spiculated solid RUL pulmonary lesion, status post robotic-assisted bronchoscopic biopsy and EBUS-guided nodal staging.  
**Anesthesia:** General anesthesia with an 8.0-mm endotracheal tube. The patient was paralyzed for robotic navigation and imaging confirmation.

**Procedures performed:** Flexible bronchoscopy, Noah Medical Galaxy robotic-assisted bronchoscopy with computer-assisted navigation, 3-D intraprocedural imaging confirmation (DT + fixed CBCT), Radial probe endobronchial ultrasound, Transbronchial needle aspiration of peripheral lung lesion, Transbronchial forceps biopsy, Linear EBUS with transbronchial needle aspiration of lymph nodes.

## Findings and procedure

The central airways were patent without visible tumor. Mild diffuse bronchitic change and small amounts of mucoid secretion were present and cleared with suction.

Robotic navigation with the Galaxy system was directed to the RUL posterior segment (RB2) target using the preplanned CT pathway. Distal airway access was achieved without resistance, and the working channel was aligned toward the lesion before confirmation imaging.

**Peripheral lesion localization:** The target measured approximately 8 mm on the planning CT and was described as spiculated solid; a bronchus sign was present. Radial EBUS showed a mixed concentric/eccentric signal after minor catheter adjustment.

**Imaging confirmation:** Digital tomosynthesis (DT) initially suggested an eccentric tool position. Fixed-room cone-beam CT (CBCT) confirmed the needle at the peripheral edge of the lesion. The catheter was adjusted several millimeters and repeat fluoroscopic views demonstrated improved alignment; a second CBCT acquisition confirmed a center-strike position.

**Sampling:** Tissue acquisition followed confirmation imaging and included transbronchial needle aspiration and multiple transbronchial forceps biopsies. Sampling was repeated from the central and peripheral portions of the image-defined target when feasible.

**Rapid on-site evaluation:** ROSE from the peripheral target demonstrated malignant gland-forming cells; final classification was deferred to permanent sections.

**Mediastinal/hilar staging:** Linear EBUS staging was performed after peripheral sampling. Stations 4L, 7, and 11L were sampled with three needle passes per station. ROSE showed lymphoid tissue without malignant cells.

**Specimens:** RUL lesion TBNA for cytology/cell block; RUL lesion forceps biopsies for surgical pathology; EBUS-TBNA lymph node specimens by station.

## Complications

There was no clinically significant bleeding, pneumothorax, hypoxemia, hemodynamic instability, or other immediate complication.

## Impression

1. Successful Noah Galaxy robotic-assisted navigation to the RUL posterior segment (RB2) pulmonary lesion with intraprocedural confirmation using DT + fixed CBCT.
2. Peripheral lesion sampled using multimodality bronchoscopic biopsy techniques.
3. Linear EBUS staging was completed with lymphoid tissue and no malignant cells identified on ROSE from sampled stations.
4. Immediate procedural complication: none.
5. Synthetic downstream pathology label for dataset use: **metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma**.

## Disposition

The patient was awakened and transferred to recovery in stable condition. A post-procedure chest radiograph was obtained when clinically indicated.
